intro: You can use Google Sheets for e-commerce merchandisers on Mac by leveraging browser-based workflows to manage large product catalogs and sales reports. Since Google Sheets runs entirely in your browser, your Mac handles it as a standard web application, allowing you to bridge the gap between Shopify exports and your internal reporting.
tldr: Google Sheets is a browser tool, so it works the same on macOS as any other system.
Install it as a Progressive Web App to keep your spreadsheets in a separate window.
Use keyboard shortcuts to move faster between product rows and inventory cells.
Lazur helps you find settings and remember formulas while you work in your browser.
Clean data is the key to accurate merchandising and inventory planning.

blocks.text: Setting up your Mac workspace for Google Sheets

Since Google Sheets lacks a native Mac app, you should use the Chrome browser to create a dedicated window. This prevents your spreadsheets from getting buried in your browser tabs. Open your sheet in Chrome, click the three-dot menu, go to Cast, Save, and Share, then select Install page as app. This creates a shortcut in your Launchpad or Applications folder. It acts like a native app and sits in your Dock.

Merchandisers often handle massive lists of SKUs. Using your mouse for everything slows you down. Press ⌘ + / to open the shortcut menu. If you need to hide old seasonal product columns, select the columns and use ⌘ + ⌥ + 0. To hide rows of discontinued items, use ⌘ + ⌥ + 9. Keep your hands on the keyboard to maintain your flow while updating inventory counts.

You likely deal with duplicate product entries from different suppliers. Use the built-in tools to clean these up. Before you start, check your data for consistency. Use the Find and Replace tool with ⌘ + ⇧ + H to standardize naming conventions like changing 'Small' to 'S' across your entire catalog. This keeps your inventory reports readable and accurate.

Google Sheets now supports up to 20 million cells. While this is a massive increase, performance can still drop if you have too many complex formulas on one page. If you notice lag, consider moving older sales data to a separate archive sheet. Use ImportRange to pull only the necessary summary data into your active planning sheet. This keeps your main file fast and responsive.

blocks.text: Your daily work involves moving data between Shopify and your reports. Create a standard export format. Import your CSV files using File > Import to ensure the data aligns with your existing columns. If you find yourself doing the same task every day, look for ways to use simple formulas to automate the math. This saves time for the creative parts of your role.
When to ask Lazur for help

Lazur lives in your Mac notch. When you get stuck, hold ⌥ + ⌘ and ask for the location of a button or the syntax for a formula. If you are tired of typing repetitive product descriptions, hold fn to dictate them directly into your sheet. Lazur helps you stay focused on your merchandising strategy instead of fighting with the interface.

faq.question: Is there an official Google Sheets app for Mac?
faq.answer: No, there is no official native app. You can create a Progressive Web App shortcut in Chrome, which gives you a dedicated window and icon in your Dock.

faq.question: How do I speed up a slow spreadsheet?
faq.answer: Reduce the number of complex formulas, delete unused rows or columns, and move historical data to an archive file. Ensure you are using the latest version of Chrome.

faq.question: Can I use Google Sheets offline?
faq.answer: Yes, you can enable offline access in your Google Drive settings. This allows you to work without an internet connection, and your changes will sync when you are back online.
